newsitem.title: FINLAND: ASKO SEEKS GROWTH FOR PIPES UNIT - CEO.
newsitem.headline: ASKO SEEKS GROWTH FOR PIPES UNIT - CEO.

text.p: After a stream of divestments, Finnish mulitibusiness group Asko Oy is seeking aggressive growth for its plastic pipes unit Uponor through investments and acquisitions, Asko's CEO said on Thursday.
"We are implementing an accelerated growth strategy for Uponor which includes investments and acquisitions," CEO Jarmo Rytilahti told a news briefing on Asko's first tertial results.
Uponor's first tertial net sales showed 8.6 percent growth to 1.20 billion markka and accounted for roughly 54 percent of total group sales.
Uponor's operating profit rose 6.2 percent to 39.7 million markka and was some 32 percent of the total operating profit.
Of the group's total investments in the first four months of 1997, about 70 percent or 82 million markka focused on Uponor.
Rytilahti said Uponor's secret to a steady success, although operating in the highly cyclical construction business, was high-quality and technologically advanced pipes.

"We do not manufacture bulk pipes ... our pipes are top-quality designer goods," he said, adding: "We have earned our position as number one in the Nordic countries and number two in Europe through craftmanship."
The outlook for Uponor in the second half of the year was steady with construction expected to pick-up in the Nordic region, one of Uponor's main markets.
Rytilahti repated earlier statements that the group's restructuring programme through asset sales was not yet complete and the aim was still to free funds and develop core businesses.
